summary: Kaniksu National Forest tower near Clark Fork: a 40-foot L-4 cab tower built in 1930, abandoned by 1951, now ruins; hike-in site.

facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1951; the sources describe ruins, not a standing tower.

visit.trail_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts calls the site a hike-in location with ruins.

events.note: Abandoned in 1951; firelookout.com lists ruins from the same year

evidence.supports: 1930 40-foot L-4 tower on the westernmost end of the summit, ruins 1951
evidence.quote: 1930: 40' L-4 tower atop westernmost end 1/3 mile southwest of summit. Ruins 1951.

evidence.supports: about 13 miles north-northeast of Clark Fork
Forest Fire Lookout Association list marks the tower gone, at the record coordinates in its list

corrections.why: The Forest Fire Lookout Association list gives 48.32540, -116.10125, which the record's own conflict list also attributes to firelookout.com. The current Idaho Fire Lookouts point is about 1.9 km away. Human check advised before applying.

notes_for_editor: Built and abandoned dates agree across all three pages, but two of them cite the same Kresek inventory, so the agreement is not fully independent. Summit elevation differs: 6,099 ft (firelookout.com) vs 6,349 ft (Idaho Fire Lookouts). Location: the record point (48.33799, -116.08378) is about 1.9 km from the FFLA list and firelookout.com point (48.3254, -116.10125); a correction is proposed for human review. Staffing: no documented staffing history on any page, so none is stated. The Idaho Fire Lookouts page has a 1970 photo caption (Stan Meyers Collection) naming Forest Service staff from the Clark Fork Ranger District; the caption does not say the photo shows this tower and no image URL was captured, so no photo is added.
